Atlanta can seek intermediate production through Kyle Pitts against Tampa Bay's weaker middle-of-field results; pace is unverified rather than assumed fast.

data_check.notes: Reads were formed from script, workload and matchup before testing the listed lines. Irving sensitivity check: 18 carries at Atlanta's allowed 4.04 YPC produces 72.72 yards, narrowly above 70.5; this is arithmetic, not a player projection. Pitts sensitivity check: five targets at his aggregate L3 124/18 receiving yards per target produces 34.44 yards, just below 34.5. His hypothesized matchup uplift therefore matters, and the read is flagged rather than treated as a clear edge. These aggregates do not establish outcome probabilities. No simulation or calibrated model was run. At -114 Irving requires approximately 53.27% to break even; at -112.5 Pitts requires approximately 52.94%. Neither number is a no-vig fair probability.

pre_mortem: Irving: Tampa Bay can be a slight favorite and still trail for much of the game. Gainwell and Tucker already have meaningful recent carries, and Atlanta's 4.04 YPC allowed leaves little margin if Irving gets only 18 attempts; unknown health or workload limits could erase the volume premise. Pitts: middle-field defensive weakness does not prove Pitts will receive those targets, and his five-target efficiency check does not clear the line. London remains Atlanta's target leader, while missing route and coverage assignments prevent confirming Pitts as the beneficiary. The counter-case is substantial enough to keep Pitts flagged and both candidates below strong confidence.

These are two research candidates, not a priced or approved parlay; do not manufacture a third leg, add touchdowns or assume independent leg probabilities.
